title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: all directors and employees of Regis Resources and its subsidiaries
tiers.description: Every director and employee of Regis Resources and its subsidiaries, plus contractors who are Restricted Persons. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the ban on short-term trading, discretionary restricted trading periods notified by the Company, and the prohibition on trading in other companies' securities while holding price sensitive information about them. Not subject to the closed periods, the funding arrangements cap or any notification obligation unless they are also a Restricted Person, director or Key Management Personnel.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001); contractors notified in writing by the Managing Director or Company Secretary; and any person designated by the Managing Director as Key Management Personnel. Restricted Persons are the only tier barred from buying or selling Company securities in the closed periods, and the only tier that can seek a Chairman's waiver in exceptional circumstances.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Automatically Restricted Persons together with their spouses and related parties. Must lodge a Trading Notification form with the Company Secretary within 2 days of buying or selling, and must promptly disclose to the Company Secretary the information the Company needs for its ASX notification within 5 business days of any change in their relevant interests. Subject to the 3% funding arrangements cap.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Any person designated by the Managing Director as key management personnel from time to time and notified in writing by the Company Secretary, and who may be de-designated on notice. Likely to include those with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities and those involved in key financial, corporate or technical activities. Restricted Persons, subject to the Trading Notification form and to the 3% funding arrangements cap.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of directors and employees, such as family members, family trusts and family companies. Directors' spouses and related parties as defined in the Corporations Act are expressly within the definition of Restricted Persons.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion notify all directors and employees that a restricted trading period is in effect and they must refrain from trading during that period. The policy does not say whether the reason is disclosed or whether the existence of the period is confidential. Key Management Personnel are identified by the Managing Director as necessary and notified in writing by the Company Secretary as being affected by the closed period. Restricted Persons are also separately barred whenever they know results are likely to differ materially from guidance, a confidential incomplete price sensitive proposal exempt under Listing Rule 3.1A is on foot, or there is information about definition drilling, resource or reserve upgrades, new discoveries or the award of a major contract.

rules.detail: The policy never mentions derivatives, options over the Company written by third parties, warrants or any equivalent. Its operative restrictions are framed as 'buying or selling Company securities' and 'trading in the Company's securities', with the only references to options being Company-issued employee options and, in the funding arrangements clause, 'their interests in the Company's shares or options'. There is no definition of trading, dealing or securities, so an OTC put or call written by a bank is not clearly caught by the closed periods.

There is no hedging clause of any kind. The policy pre-dates the hedging restrictions now standard in ASX policies and says nothing about limiting the economic risk of unvested plan securities or performance rights. Any hedging restriction would have to come from the Employee Share Option Plan rules or remuneration documents, which are not part of this policy.

Hedging vested unrestricted shares is likewise unaddressed. The only constraints that could bite are the insider trading prohibition, the undefined short-term trading ban, the closed periods (which are framed as buying or selling securities) and, for directors and Key Management Personnel, the 3% funding arrangements cap.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and equivalent structures are not mentioned. A monetisation that is funded and secured on Company shares would engage the funding arrangements cap in 4.12 for directors and Key Management Personnel if the security reached 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere. Only the general short-term trading exhortation and the insider trading laws would apply.
Securities lending or borrowing is not mentioned and there is no definition of trading that would capture it.
Contracts for difference are not mentioned and there is no definition of securities or financial products that would sweep them in.

Margin lending is not banned as such. The only restriction is a size test: a funding arrangement relating to a director's interests in Company shares or options is prohibited where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares. Below that threshold no approval, notification or condition is imposed on the loan itself.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: Identical 3% funding security cap for Key Management Personnel designated by the Managing Director. Employees who are neither directors nor designated Key Management Personnel are not caught by 4.12 at all.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company shares or options is regulated only through 4.12, and only by reference to the size of the funding security relative to the Company's listed shares. A charge or pledge is not otherwise a dealing and needs no clearance; there is no requirement to disclose the arrangement to the Company.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: The scope is broad in kind but narrow in effect: any funding arrangement relating to a director's interests in Company shares or options is caught, but only where the funding security reaches the 3% threshold. There is no prohibition below the threshold, no approval gateway, no distinction by vesting state and no forced-sale provision.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: Same 3% threshold applies to Key Management Personnel. The policy does not say how the 3% is measured, whether it aggregates across facilities or associates, or when it is tested.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: An undefined ban on short-term trading expressed as a 'should never' obligation, with no period specified and no measurement basis. The only carve-out is the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.tier: all directors and employees of Regis Resources and its subsidiaries
clearance.evidence: The Company Secretary will endeavour to notify all Directors, employees and any other Restricted Persons of the times when they are permitted to buy or sell the Company's securities.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (Trading Notification form, including number of securities, date and whether the trading occurred inside a closed period); and prompt disclosure of the information required for the Company's ASX notification of a change in relevant interests
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days after buying or selling; ASX notification by the Company within 5 business days
clearance.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel must complete a Trading Notification form and provide it to the Company Secretary within 2 days after that person buys or sells securities in the Company.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days after buying or selling
clearance.evidence: The Trading Notification form must be completed in full, including details of the number of securities traded, the date the trading took place and whether the trading occurred inside a closed period.

clearance.approver: Chairman (Trading Exemption Request form submitted to the Company Secretary); applies only to waivers of the closed periods in 4.3 and the restricted trading periods in 4.4
clearance.evidence: The Restricted Person must satisfy the Chairman that the circumstances are exceptional and that the proposed sale or disposal of the securities is the only reasonable course of action available to them and must submit a Trading Exemption Request form seeking authorisation of the trade to the Company Secretary. Any such clearance will be provided in writing (including by email).

carve_outs: the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares;
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class;
acquire or agree to acquire or exercise options under the Company's Employee Share Option Plan;
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer;
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, on a Trading Exemption Request form submitted to the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: In specific circumstances such as severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances, the Chairman may waive the trading restrictions in paragraphs 4.3 - 4.4 on the condition that the Restricted Person can demonstrate that they are not in possession of any price sensitive information that is generally not available to the public.
Other examples of "exceptional circumstances" include a transfer of shares required by family court order or other legal requirement.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance. The single financing control is a size cap measured against the Company's whole issued capital: 'funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares'. The policy does not say how or when the 3% is measured, whether facilities or associates aggregate, or what happens if the threshold is crossed after inception through a fall in the share count.

exemption_authority: The Chairman may waive the closed period restrictions in 4.3 and the discretionary restricted trading periods in 4.4 in specific circumstances such as severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (including a transfer of shares required by family court order or other legal requirement), conditional on the Restricted Person demonstrating they hold no price sensitive information and satisfying the Chairman that the proposed sale or disposal is the only reasonable course of action available. A Trading Exemption Request form goes to the Company Secretary and clearance is given in writing including by email. There is no authority to waive the short-term trading ban in 4.5 or the funding arrangements cap in 4.12.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only financing control in the policy: a funded collar is permissible for directors and KMP provided the security package stays below 3% of Regis's listed shares, with no approval, disclosure or condition otherwise imposed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no hedging clause, no derivatives clause, no short selling clause and no definition of dealing, trading or securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is expressly restricted, but the absence of drafting also means there is no clearance mechanism through which a bank can obtain company comfort that the structure is compliant.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restrictions framed as buying or selling
bespoke_clauses.clause: All Restricted Persons are prohibited from buying or selling Company securities: in the 14 day period prior to the release of the half yearly results announcement to ASX ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The closed periods are expressed as a bar on buying or selling Company securities, so on a literal reading entering an OTC option with a bank is not caught, though physical settlement or a collateral transfer plainly would be.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary will endeavour to notify all Directors, employees and any other Restricted Persons of the times when they are permitted to buy or sell the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no pre-clearance requirement for ordinary dealing, only notification of permitted times, so a bank cannot rely on a company approval as evidence the structure was sanctioned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The notification must also specify whether the trading took place during a closed period, where prior written clearance was required, and if so, when that was provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ASX notification clause assumes a prior written clearance process that the policy never establishes outside the exceptional circumstances route, so the practical process should be confirmed with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel must complete a Trading Notification form and provide it to the Company Secretary within 2 days after that person buys or sells securities in the Company. The Trading Notification form must be completed in full, including details of the number of securities traded, the date the trading took place and whether the trading occurred inside a closed period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physical delivery or on-market leg of the collar triggers a two day notification and, for directors, a Company ASX filing within five business days if relevant interests change.

bespoke_clauses.clause: there exists information regarding definition drilling, resource or reserve upgrades or new discoveries or the awarding of any major contract or relating to other activities such as those set out in clause 3.5 of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Exploration and resource news flow creates frequent open-ended trading bars for Restricted Persons that are not tied to a calendar, so execution dates cannot be planned reliably.

bespoke_clauses.topic: spouses and related parties are Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons means: all directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001);
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking a collar through a director's spouse, family trust or related party does not escape the closed periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no stated period, so the tenor risk is unquantifiable and a bank should assume a conservative minimum such as twelve months and avoid early unwind features.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities Trading Policy (applicable from 31 December 2010). Last updated: 23 December 2010.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This policy is from 2010, pre-dates the hedging and margin lending provisions now standard in ASX policies, and no review cycle is stated, so the bank must verify whether a current version exists before relying on the silences.

summary: On its face a funded collar is available to Regis directors and executives, because this 2010 policy is silent on hedging, derivatives, short selling and stock lending, and its only financing control is a size cap: directors and Key Management Personnel must not enter funding arrangements relating to their interests in Company shares or options where the funding security would affect 3% or more of the Company's listed shares. The derivative legs are not expressly regulated at all, and the closed periods (14 days before half year, full year and disclosure document announcements, 7 days before quarterlies, plus discretionary restricted trading periods and open-ended bars tied to drilling, resource upgrades or major contracts) are drafted as a bar on buying or selling Company securities, so entry into an OTC option is arguably outside them while physical settlement or a collateral transfer clearly is not. The practical obstacles are the absence of any pre-clearance mechanism through which the company could bless the structure, the undefined 'should never engage in short-term trading' ban, and the two day Trading Notification and five business day ASX disclosure obligations for directors and KMP on any purchase or sale. Because the policy is silent rather than permissive, the bank should not treat the silences as consent: any hedging restriction is more likely to sit in the Employee Share Option Plan and remuneration documents, which are outside this policy. Given the policy dates from December 2010 with no stated review cycle, its currency should be confirmed before relying on it.
